title: Cross-module automation platform
summary: Build durable Journeys that respond to CRM, test-drive, stock, workshop, warranty, support, portal, document and Xero lifecycle events.

body.text: Journeys are the main cross-module automation engine. They are versioned, durable and tenant-scoped. Quick rules remain available for simple one-step lead actions, but new multi-step workflows should be built as Journeys.

items: Immediate events include test-drive booking/completion/no-show, quote sent/opened, stock receiving and inspection, PDI, delivery scheduling, job-card lifecycle, warranty and recalls, support cases, portal requests and document approval.
Time-based triggers include overdue activities, expiring quotes, delayed deliveries, service due, expiring warranties, overdue cases and stalled signature requests.
The Xero invoice-status trigger is exposed as an integration contract. It activates when the Xero connector records a changed status.
Messaging actions send email, SMS, WhatsApp, staff push notifications and portal notifications.
Operational actions create activities, support cases, job cards, workshop bookings, approval requests, stock-transfer requests and test-drive follow-ups.
Governance actions use a safe field whitelist, tenant staff validation and visible approval/queue records.
Integration actions include signed HTTPS webhooks, generated documents, signature requests and Xero draft-invoice requests.

body.text: Open Automations → Approvals to make internal decisions. Open Automations → Action queue to inspect document, signing and integration work. Failed work can be retried; blocked Xero actions remain visible until the Xero integration is connected.

DenagoCRM never turns Xero actions into internal accounting. The CRM may request a draft invoice and receive its operational status, while Xero remains responsible for invoices, tax, payments and the ledger.
